I have analyzed the test image. The image displays a close-up of a plant stem and leaves. The most prominent feature is a section of the stem that appears bleached and tan-colored. There is a fluffy, white mycelial growth covering parts of the stem lesion. Additionally, there are hard, black sclerotia, which resemble small rodent droppings, embedded within the white mold and on the stem surface. The leaves show signs of wilting and discoloration, turning from a grayish-green to brown.

Based on the provided knowledge base, these symptoms align most closely with the description for **White_Mold**. The key diagnostic features mentioned are: "Lesions usually develop first at stem nodes... Infected stems often become soft and watery, covered with white moldy growth in moist conditions, or develop a bleached white appearance when dry." and most importantly, "Hard, black sclerotia that resemble rodent droppings develop on or inside infected stems and pods; white fluffy mycelium covers stem lesions under moist conditions." The image clearly shows the white, fluffy mycelium and the distinctive black sclerotia on the stem.
